    assert days_in_month(1900, 2) == 28


def test_median_even_length():
    assert median([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2.5
    assert median([5, 1]) == 3
    assert median([10, 2, 8, 4]) == 6

    assert days_in_month(2024, 2) == 29
    assert days_in_month(2023, 2) == 28

        days_in_month(2023, 13)

text: All 15 tests pass. Let me clean up my helper script:

All 15 tests now pass (previously 12 passed, 3 failed). The three bugs and their fixes:

1. **`toolkit/dates.py` — `is_leap_year`**: Only checked divisibility by 4, so century years like 1900 were wrongly reported as leap years. Fixed with the full Gregorian rule: `year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)`.

2. **`toolkit/stats.py` — `median`**: Always returned `s[n // 2]`, which is wrong for even-length lists. Fixed to average the two middle values when the length is even: `(s[n//2 - 1] + s[n//2]) / 2`.

3. **`toolkit/text.py` — `title_case`**: Used `str.title()`, which capitalizes letters after apostrophes (`"It'S A Dog'S Life"`). Replaced with a regex-based implementation that capitalizes only the first character of each word and lowercases the rest, preserving apostrophes correctly.

No changes were made under `tests/`, and all previously passing tests still pass.
